headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can write/egress broadly while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress, creating default data-leakage and capability-conflict exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads and writes VS Code workspace files and can use MCP, so it may ingest content from nuwa-skill outputs if they are placed in the shared workspace. nuwa-skill has no documented shared channel, but the filesystem bridge makes prompt injection plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill output is copied into the shared VS Code workspace
IF Roo Code is configured to treat workspace files or MCP payloads as instructions
mitigations: Keep agent outputs in separate directories
Disable MCP for untrusted workspaces
Add a fixed instruction delimiter in files
Review any file imported from nuwa-skill before Roo Code reads it

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code has broad network egress and handles workspace files and browser screenshots; nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive source code or screenshots can flow into Roo Code’s model/API calls. The pair lacks documented isolation, so the shared-workspace leakage path is credible.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same VS Code workspace
IF Roo Code sends workspace contents or screenshots to a configured model API or MCP server
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent
Remove secrets from shared files before Roo Code runs
Restrict Roo Code network targets to approved endpoints
Turn off screen capture when handling sensitive material

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses in a workspace-shared concurrency model. nuwa-skill has network egress and may also act on repository content. With no locking or coordination documented, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git state by default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or workspace
IF either agent performs writes without an external lock
mitigations: Assign one agent per repository checkout
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees for parallel work
Require manual review before commits

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on workspace content and modify git state, so if it consumes nuwa-skill output as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or commits. nuwa-skill is a research agent with allowlisted egress, but no verification loop between the pair is documented, so the handoff is risky though not automatically destructive.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses nuwa-skill output as a source of truth
IF Roo Code commits or edits files based on that output without human verification
mitigations: Require a human review step before commits
Mark nuwa-skill outputs as untrusted notes
Ask Roo Code to cite file paths before acting
Use read-only mode for the research handoff

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for nuwa-skill or Roo Code, so compliance risk is limited to generic policy gaps. I cite both profiles because the pairwise assessment depends on their data handling and egress surfaces, but there is no specific regulated-data pathway shown.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF organizational policy forbids model/API transmission of that data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Disable network egress for sensitive sessions
Use a separate compliant environment
Review retention settings before use
